issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSong(): the problem statement (UML and textual description) and the template declare/describe singFarmSong() as a void method that prints the song to System.out, but the solution repository implements singFarmSong() with return type String (and its helper singFarmSongVerse(...) also returns String). This mismatch (void vs String) creates real ambiguity for students: should they implement singFarmSong() to print the song (void) as instructed by the exercise and template, or return the full song as a String as shown in the solution? Tests and grading may expect one behaviour and not the other.
issues.suggestedFix:
Pick one consistent contract and apply it across problem text, template, tests, and solution. Two viable options:
1) Align with the problem statement and template: change the solution to implement public void singFarmSong() that prints the song to System.out. If the helper returns a String, ensure the public method prints that String; or change the helper to void and print the verse directly.
2) If returning the full song String is desired, update the problem statement (UML and text) and the template signature to declare singFarmSong() as returning String and document that students should return the composed song text (and update tests accordingly).
Make the chosen contract explicit in the problem statement and in the template Java signature so students are not left to reconcile conflicting examples in the solution code.
